solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Monkey beginning to descend tropical tree

parts.note: the tamarin is a small South American monkey

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word supplies just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A monkey starts climbing down from a tree in the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a leguminous tree of tropical Africa and Asia, grown for its sour pods.

clue.text: Patient sorting of silver, dividing incomplete samples

indicators.note: the silver symbol splits the other word in two
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: tries means samples, as when tasting
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A hospital sorts patients while splitting up partial specimens of silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like an adjective (calm) but qualifies 'sorting' as a noun: the sorting of patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Assigning priority to the sick or wounded by urgency is the sorting of patients in an emergency.

clue.text: Revolutionary Soviet cum "capitalist"

definitions.note: here read playfully as a resident of a capital city

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A revolutionary Russian who is also, oddly, a capitalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalist' is in quotes because it means someone from a capital, here Moscow, not a believer in capitalism.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Moscow, the Russian capital, is a capital dweller in the punning sense.

clue.text: One isolated from Conservative Left entering new employment

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the other word

parts.note: reuse means putting to new use

explanation.surface: A politician cut off from the Tories and the left takes up a new job.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hermit, someone who lives apart from society.

clue.text: Possible source of drugs turned up E's and whizz

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from the bottom

parts.note: Es are ecstasy tablets
to whizz is to run fast

explanation.surface: Ecstasy and speed (whizz is slang for amphetamine) appear as possible origins of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ESRUN in this down entry. The surface plays on whizz as slang for amphetamine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital staff on a ward hand out medication, so one may supply you with drugs.

clue.text: Exile foreign ruler possessing good English

indicators.note: the ruler holds the next letter inside himself

parts.note: an emir is a Muslim ruler or prince

explanation.surface: An overseas potentate who speaks fine English has been banished.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an émigré is someone who has left their homeland, often for political reasons, much like an exile.

clue.text: Digger's long period in American's shed

definitions.note: the apostrophe S stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the period goes inside the shedding word

parts.note: molt is the American spelling of moult, to shed
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A digger spends ages in a Yank's garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing African rodent spends its life tunnelling, so it is a natural excavator.

clue.text: Excessive desire to have browser — Google's first up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom

parts.note: a deer browses on leaves and shoots

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the search giant's name is used

explanation.surface: Someone is desperate to own the web browser that Google makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browser' suggests web software but means a grazing animal; 'up' reverses DEERG.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: avarice, an excessive desire for more than one needs.

clue.text: Grounds for incarcerating one male judge

indicators.note: the grounds lock up the letters inside them

parts.note: an estate is grounds belonging to a large house
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Reasons for a judge jailing a man.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to reckon or assess roughly, which is to judge an amount.

clue.text: Cephalonia's interior is steaming — get as far from the sun as possible

definitions.text: as far from the sun as possible
definitions.note: describes the point of a planet's orbit most distant from the sun

indicators.note: steaming suggests wild agitation, so the letters are churned
the interior is the word without its outer letters

explanation.surface: Inland Cephalonia, a Greek island, is sweltering, so you want distance from the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior' drops the outer C and A to give EPHALONI, which 'is steaming' rearranges. 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers name the orbital point farthest from the sun with this term.

clue.text: Sleeper in tent with 150 flies around? You need this!

definitions.text: Sleeper in tent with 150 flies around? You need this!

indicators.note: the letters fly about and land in a new order

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A camper sleeping under canvas, plagued by a swarm of flies, is told what to bring.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a camper beset by flies needs exactly this. 'flies' is both the anagram signal and the pests.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray or cream that keeps bugs away is what anyone sleeping under canvas amid swarms would want.

clue.text: Drop litres in mouth before Christmas, when year's out

indicators.note: the first part comes before the second in the answer
the litres abbreviation goes inside the word for mouth

parts.note: gob is British slang for mouth

indicators.note: the abbreviation for year is taken away from the festive word

parts.note: Yule is an old name for Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone pours a few litres down their throat ahead of the holidays as the year ends.
explanation.walkthrough: GOB is everyday British slang for mouth. Removing Y from YULE leaves ULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small spherical drop of liquid, such as a bead of oil or sweat.

clue.text: What may come with making me a lord

definitions.text: What may come with making me a lord

indicators.note: making signals the letters of the next words are fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what perks follow being raised to the peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges ME A LORD; read whole, the clue describes the rank and title that go with being ennobled.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank or territory of a peer of that grade is exactly what comes with being ennobled as one.

clue.text: Some mathematical iterations, they ought to be learned

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Repeated calculations are a skill educated people are expected to have mastered.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia are educated, well-read people, so they are by reputation learned.

clue.text: Renegade contessa finally set for the future without duke

indicators.note: finally selects the last letter of the word
the word goes without the duke's letter

parts.note: to postdate is to assign a later date

explanation.surface: A countess has finally fixed future plans without the duke.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing D from POSTDATE leaves POSTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who abandons a religious or political allegiance is a turncoat.

clue.text: Foul rubbish gathering at home

indicators.note: the rubbish word gathers the home word into its middle

parts.note: tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Junk piling up around the house is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT is everyday British slang for tawdry junk.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to contaminate or pollute something, which is what fouling it means.

clue.text: Warm corner in valley by old well

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland
OK means well, as in feeling fine

explanation.surface: A cosy spot in a valley beside an ancient spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like a water source but means fine or all right.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug recess beside a large open fireplace is a warm corner of the room.

clue.text: Boiling uniform with fastening sleeves

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pin fastens things together
the sleeves of a garment are its arms

explanation.surface: A hot uniform with buttoned cuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being furious or protesting strongly is figuratively boiling with anger.

clue.text: City's losing to Newcastle initially, bringing crowd together

indicators.note: the city loses a run of letters from its middle

parts.note: Preston is a city in Lancashire, with the possessive S
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A football club fails against Newcastle early on, which brings the fans together.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESTON is a city in Lancashire, England, whose club plays Newcastle. Taking TO and N out of PRESTONS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to throng or push in a mass, as a crowd presses forward.

clue.text: Design aid: tool for drawing street for page

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, the street replacing the page

parts.note: a pencil is a tool for drawing

explanation.surface: A list of graphic equipment: a drawing implement swapped for a sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-out template used to reproduce a pattern is an aid to designing.

clue.text: Knocked back unknown gloop outside solitary drinker's study?

indicators.note: knocking back a drink suggests the whole assembly is read in reverse

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: the gloop surrounds the solitary word

parts.note: goo is sticky gloop
lone means solitary

explanation.surface: A lone tippler downs a glass of something murky.
explanation.walkthrough: The assembled string before reversal is YGOLONEO. The question mark flags that a wine buff is only one kind of drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of wine is a study a wine drinker might pursue, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Wash three articles from the Continent

parts.note: LA is the French feminine article for 'the'
UN is the French masculine article for 'a'
DER is the German masculine article for 'the'

explanation.surface: A tourist cleans three items picked up abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to wash and iron clothes or linen.

clue.text: Soul singer's lead part in Evita

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the surname

parts.note: Evita was the nickname of Eva Perón, wife of the Argentine president

indicators.note: the lead part of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A soul singer lands the lead role in the musical Evita.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soul' suggests the music genre but is the definition, meaning a human being.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as in 'not a soul in sight', a soul is an individual human.

clue.text: Dawning of new progressive movement

parts.note: an ascent is a steady movement upwards

explanation.surface: The birth of a fresh political current on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: just coming into being, the way a day is beginning at dawn.

clue.text: Stint as captain stretching over months

indicators.note: the captain's word stretches around the month letter

parts.note: a skip or skipper is a team captain

explanation.surface: A spell as team leader lasting several months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stint' looks like a noun, a spell of duty, but is the verb: to be sparing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to economise or be stingy with something, as in stinting on food.

clue.text: Novelist halved year's rest

parts.note: Nevil Shute was an English novelist, author of A Town Like Alice

indicators.note: only the front half of the following word is kept

explanation.surface: A writer cut his annual output and took a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal idiom for sleep, the most restful of rests.

clue.text: Charming American uplifted by welcome

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the letters up means reading them backwards

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail or welcome

explanation.surface: A delightful American cheered by a warm greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: smooth and urbane in manner, as a charming person is.

clue.text: Bucket contains rags dad recycled

indicators.note: recycled signals the letters are reprocessed into a new form

explanation.surface: A pail holds old rags that father has put out for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucket' looks like a pail, but here it is the verb: to pour down heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for a heavy downpour of rain.

clue.text: Serve without stiffness

definitions.meaning: to provide or furnish something needed
the adverb from supple, meaning in a flexible, lithe manner

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a rare adverb formed from supple, pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb to provide; the other the adverb meaning flexibly.

clue.text: Supports family making headwear

parts.note: bears means supports, as a pillar bears weight
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A family's backing results in a new hat.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the tall fur cap worn by the guards outside Buckingham Palace in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tall black fur cap worn by guardsmen is a type of headwear.
